# pgtools Helm chart

The pgToolBox **team tools** for CloudNativePG: what a team runs beside its
Clusters, in its own namespace, installed by whoever administers that namespace.

| Tool | Values | Default | What it installs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **console** | `console.enabled` | `true` | the console: one Deployment or StatefulSet (a StatefulSet with `console.history.persistent`), watching `console.watchNamespaces` |
| **insight pack** | `insightPack.enabled` | `true` | the ConfigMap `<release>-insight-pack` of CloudNativePG custom queries in each watched namespace; a Cluster uses it only once its team opts in ([below](#the-insight-pack)) |
| **evidence agents** | `evidence.agents` | none | one backup-evidence agent per listed Cluster: a Deployment, a Service, a ServiceAccount and a Role ([below](#evidence-agents-without-the-operator)) |
| **pgAdmin** | `pgadmin.enabled` | `false` | one pgAdmin for the team: a Deployment, with the servers declared in `pgadmin.servers` ([below](#pgadmin-without-the-operator)) |

```bash
helm install pgtoolbox-console charts/pgtools --namespace team-a \
  --set console.auth.provider=token
```

The chart renders **no CRD** and, by default, **nothing cluster-scoped**: an admin of
the namespace can install it (`make helm-unittest` proves the default render holds
only namespaced kinds). Two optional pieces add a ClusterRole, both off by default:
`console.clusterImageCatalogs.enabled` and `console.metrics.readerClusterRole`.

Kubernetes lets a user grant only the rights they hold, and the chart's Roles grant
read on the team's PostgreSQL objects. So the installing user needs, in the
namespace:

- the built-in `admin` ClusterRole (bound with a RoleBinding);
- `get`, `list` and `watch` on the CloudNativePG kinds (`postgresql.cnpg.io`) and on
  `objectstores` (`barmancloud.cnpg.io`). CloudNativePG does not add them to
  `admin`; a team that owns its Clusters usually holds them already.

Where the pgtoolbox operator is installed, the console also links to its
`PgAdmin`, `EvidenceAgent` and `PgAccessRequest` objects. The operator chart adds
read on them to `admin` (`pgtoolbox-aggregate-to-admin`), and
`console.rbac.operatorKinds: auto` grants it only where the cluster serves those
kinds. With `helm template` (Argo CD), there is no discovery: set it `true` beside
the operator.

### What you give up without the operator

The pgtoolbox chart's operator keeps a team's tools in step with what exists in the
cluster. Here the values are the whole truth:

- the watched namespaces are `console.watchNamespaces`, read at install; a new
  namespace is a `helm upgrade`;
- nothing is created for you when a Cluster appears: the console sees it (it lists
  Clusters through its Role), the other tools see what their values name;
- the console image is the chart's: upgrading it is upgrading the release;
- the two user ClusterRoles (`pgtoolbox-console-viewer`, `pgtoolbox-console-operator`) are the
  operator chart's (`operator.userRoles.create`) or `config/rbac`'s; without them,
  grant people ordinary Roles (NOTES.txt prints an example).

## What a console is allowed to do

There is no cluster-scoped console: a console is bounded by its namespace. Its
authority is Roles in the watched namespaces and one small ClusterRole, and
nothing else.

| Object | Where | Grants |
|---|---|---|
| `Role` + `RoleBinding` `<release>-console` | each of `console.watchNamespaces` (default: the release namespace) | `get/list/watch` (informers) on the CNPG kinds (`clusters`, `backups`, `scheduledbackups`, `poolers`, `databases`, `databaseroles`, `publications`, `subscriptions`, `failoverquorums`, `imagecatalogs`), `objectstores`, `pgadmins`, `evidenceagents`, `pgaccessrequests` (only with `console.rbac.operatorKinds`; `auto`: where the operator's kinds are served), pods, PVCs, services, PDBs, leases, jobs; `list/watch` on events and resourcequotas; `get` on replicasets and deployments; `get` on `pods/log` unless `console.rbac.podLogs=false` |
| `Role` + `RoleBinding` `<release>-console-revocations` | release namespace | `get/watch` on **one** ConfigMap, by `resourceNames` (the revocation list: the console never writes it; an admin edits `notBefore`, `users`, `sessions`) |
| `ConfigMap` + `Role` + `RoleBinding` `<release>-console-state` | release namespace | `get/watch/update` on **one** ConfigMap, by `resourceNames`: the state the replicas share (sign-outs as SHA-256 hashes, "since" times, digest delivery marks), created empty and written by the console; within a namespace admin's own grants |
| `Role` + `RoleBinding` `<release>-console-digest` | release namespace, **only** with a `console.digest.delivery` channel | `get/update` on **one** Lease, `<release>-console-digest`, by `resourceNames`, and `create` on `leases`: only the replica holding the Lease delivers the digests. RBAC cannot scope `create` by name (a create is authorized before the object exists), so the console may create a Lease of any name in the release namespace; it creates only this one (pinned by `hack/readonlycheck`). Leases are in the built-in `edit` and `admin` roles: a namespace admin may grant this |
| `ClusterRole` + `ClusterRoleBinding` `<namespace>:<release>-console:clusterimagecatalogs` | cluster, **only** with `console.clusterImageCatalogs.enabled` | `get/list/watch` on `clusterimagecatalogs` |
| `ClusterRole` `<namespace>:<release>-console:metrics-reader` (+ binding to `metrics.readerSubjects`) | cluster, **only** with `console.metrics.readerClusterRole` | `get` on the non-resource URL `/metrics`; for the scraper, not the console |
| `Role` + `RoleBinding` `<release>-console-restore-drills` | the drill namespace (`console.restoreDrills.namespace`, else each watched namespace), **only** with `console.restoreDrills.enabled` | `get/list/watch/delete` on `clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io`: the teardown of the restore drills the console created |
| `NetworkPolicy` `<release>-console-restore-drills` | each drill namespace, with `console.restoreDrills.enabled` and `.networkPolicy.enabled` (default on) | the drill Pods (`drill-owner` label = the release namespace): egress to DNS, the API server and the object store only; ingress from the CloudNativePG operator and this console on the instance ports |
| `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` + binding `<release>-console-<namespace>-restore-drills` (cluster-scoped) | **only** with `console.restoreDrills.admissionPolicy.create` (a cluster admin; Kubernetes 1.30+) | the console's ServiceAccount may delete a Cluster in the drill namespaces only when it carries this console's `drill-owner` label, the drill seal annotation and the drill prefix |

No Secret verb exists anywhere, no wildcard, no `impersonate`, and no write
except the console's own state ConfigMap, its digest Lease (with delivery) and
the opt-in drill teardown. The
ServiceAccount does not automount its token; the console container gets a
projected, short-lived one. The writes the console performs (backup, reload, restart, promote and
starting a restore drill) are made with
the **user's** token, never the ServiceAccount's. The one exception is deleting a
restore drill after its check or its time limit, when the person who started it
may be gone: the console deletes only the Clusters it sealed as its own drills
(an HMAC under a key derived from its session secret, bound to the drill's
namespace and name), preconditioned on their UID; their PVCs follow through
CloudNativePG's owner references. A person who starts a drill needs `create` on
`clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io` in the drill namespace from their own RBAC; the
console's shipped user roles do not grant it. `hack/validate-packaging.sh` and the unit tests in `tests/`
enforce all of this on the rendered objects, and `make test-e2e-chart` proves it
against a real API server.

To let a person see Clusters, give them an ordinary RoleBinding in the watched
namespace (`get` on `clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io`); the console asks the API
server with a SelfSubjectAccessReview sent with their own token.

## Replicas and history: the one availability rule

* default: `console.replicas: 2`, a Deployment rolling with `maxUnavailable: 0`,
  history kept in memory, a PodDisruptionBudget (`minAvailable: 1`);
* `console.history.persistent: true`: a **StatefulSet** of `console.replicas`
  (still 2 by default), one claim of `console.history.size` per replica from a
  claim template (`history-<console>-<ordinal>`; the history file takes an
  exclusive lock, so replicas never share one), `podManagementPolicy: Parallel`,
  rolling one pod at a time, the same PodDisruptionBudget, Service, probes,
  security context and anti-affinity. The claims are deleted with the release
  and kept when scaling down. The console's name must then be at most 52
  characters (a StatefulSet's pods carry a 63-character label made from it).

Each replica keeps its own history, so `console.exposure.sticky` (on by default)
keeps a person on one replica; sign-outs and "since" times agree across
replicas anyway (the state ConfigMap).

The pgtools chart keeps `persistent: false` by default because a team namespace
may have no StorageClass. Turn it on wherever one exists: the charts, the
timeline, the digests and the "since" times then survive a roll.

### Persistent history

**Sizing.** One claim holds the history journal (up to `HISTORY_MAX_REVISIONS`
revisions, by default 5,000 of a few KiB each: tens of MiB), the timeline and
the digests (30 days by default: a few MiB) and the state snapshots. The sweep's
snapshot is the largest part: about 100 KiB per instance, so 5 MiB for 50
instances, bounded at 512 MiB (some 5,000 instances); the log matches' one is
bounded at 64 MiB. A snapshot is written beside the previous one and then
renamed, so count it twice. `1Gi` covers a console of a few hundred instances
with room to spare; above a thousand, give it `2Gi`.

**Changing the size or the class.** A StatefulSet's claim template cannot be
changed in place, so `helm upgrade` with a new `console.history.size` or
`storageClassName` is refused by the API server. Delete the StatefulSet without
its pods, then upgrade; the existing claims keep their size (grow one by editing
its PVC, if its StorageClass allows expansion), new claims take the new one:

```sh
kubectl -n <namespace> delete statefulset <console> --cascade=orphan
helm upgrade <release> pgtools -n <namespace> --reuse-values --set console.history.size=4Gi
```

## The daily digest

Each day at `console.digest.hour` (UTC, default 7) the console summarises the
last 24 hours on its `/digests` page: Cluster changes, findings that appeared,
worsened or cleared, failovers and switchovers, failed backups, restarts and the
Clusters needing attention. Digests are kept `console.digest.retention` (default
`720h`) with the history, so across restarts only with persistent history. Every
replica makes and keeps its own copy.

Delivery is **off** until a channel is set under `console.digest.delivery`
(`chat`: a Slack or Mattermost incoming webhook; `webhook`: a generic JSON
webhook; `smtp`: mail over STARTTLS or implicit TLS, never in clear). Each
credential (a webhook URL is one) is a key of a Secret you create, mounted as a
file and re-read at every attempt; the console reads no Secret through the API.
Messages carry counts, the names of Clusters needing attention and a link to
`console.publicURL`/digests/<id>, never the details. Delivery needs
`console.history.persistent: true` (the chart refuses otherwise): the message
links to the digest's page, which in-memory history loses at the next restart.
Only the replica holding the Lease `<console>-digest` delivers (`DIGEST_LEASE`);
which channel delivered which digest is shared in the state ConfigMap, so a
roll or a failover sends nothing twice and finishes what the previous holder had
not sent. A replica that stops between a send and the write of its mark (about
a second) can make the next holder send that one digest again: at least once,
never lost. With `console.networkPolicy.enabled`,
open the webhook or mail server in `console.networkPolicy.extraEgress`, as
narrowly as you can: the destination's addresses and only the ports it uses.

```yaml
console:
  networkPolicy:
    extraEgress:
      # The chat or webhook endpoint (HTTPS), or the egress proxy in front of it.
      - to:
          - ipBlock: {cidr: 203.0.113.10/32}
        ports:
          - {port: 443, protocol: TCP}
      # The mail relay: 465 (implicit TLS) or 587 (STARTTLS), whichever it uses.
      - to:
          - ipBlock: {cidr: 198.51.100.25/32}
        ports:
          - {port: 465, protocol: TCP}
          - {port: 587, protocol: TCP}
```

A rule without `to` and `ports` — `- {}` — allows **all** egress from the
console pod and defeats the policy; never use it for a digest destination.

## The `/pg/status` CA bundle (you supply it)

The console reads each instance's `/pg/status` over HTTPS and verifies it against
a bundle **you** create: a ConfigMap, `console.instanceStatus.caBundleConfigMap`
(default `pgtoolbox-console-instance-ca`), key `ca.crt`, the PEM server CAs of the watched
Clusters. The chart only mounts it; the kubelet refreshes it without a restart.
The console never reads a Secret (`<cluster>-ca` also holds `ca.key`), and a
Cluster missing from the bundle is shown as "not verifiable", never read
unverified.

```bash
# one command per Cluster; ordinary namespace RBAC is enough
for c in $(kubectl -n team-a get clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do
  kubectl -n team-a get secret "$c-ca" -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d
done > ca.crt
kubectl -n team-a create configmap pgtoolbox-console-instance-ca --from-file=ca.crt=ca.crt
```

CNPG allows a user-managed `serverCASecret` shared by all Clusters of a
namespace; the bundle then has one entry.

**A copy made once expires within 90 days.** CloudNativePG gives the CA it
creates for each Cluster 90 days of validity and renews it 7 days before expiry;
when the copied certificate expires, every instance of that Cluster reads
`tlsError`. Keep the bundle current: a cert-manager trust-manager `Bundle` that
syncs the Clusters' `ca.crt` into this ConfigMap, one long-lived user-managed
`serverCASecret` shared by the namespace's Clusters (CloudNativePG does not renew
a CA it did not create), or a console run by the operator (`PgToolBoxConsole`), which
mirrors the CAs itself. Details: the documentation's console configuration page,
"The instance CA bundle".

**Restore drills** are Clusters created after you filled the bundle, so the
console signs each one with a CA already in it
(`console.restoreDrills.serverCA`, `spec.certificates.serverCASecret` of the
drill): by default (`auto`) the source Cluster's own server CA when drills run in
the source's namespace, or, in a dedicated drill namespace, a CA Secret you
create there and name in `serverCA.secret` (add its `ca.crt` to the bundle).
CloudNativePG reads that Secret for the drill; the console still reads none and
its RBAC is unchanged.

## Authentication

`console.auth.provider`: `token` (the user pastes an API-server token, the
break-glass path that works everywhere), `oidc` or `openshift`. On vanilla
Kubernetes, SSO needs the API server to trust the IdP (`--oidc-*` flags or an
`AuthenticationConfiguration`): the token the console holds must be one the API
server accepts. The session cookie is sealed under a key the chart generates once
and keeps across upgrades (`console.auth.sessionKey.existingSecret` to bring your
own; do so under a GitOps tool that renders client-side, where `lookup` has no
cluster to ask). The OIDC client secret is a Secret you create and the chart
mounts as a file.

## Break-glass

`console.breakGlass.enabled=true` renders the identity behind the token login form: a
ServiceAccount `pgtoolbox-console-breakglass` that holds no token and mounts nothing, and in each
watched namespace a RoleBinding to the `pgtoolbox-console-operator` ClusterRole (which must
exist: the pgtoolbox chart's `operator.userRoles.create`, or `kubectl apply -k config/rbac`).
Without the operator that ClusterRole does not exist, and a namespace admin cannot create
one: set `console.breakGlass.roleKind=Role` and the chart renders, in each watched
namespace, a Role named like the ServiceAccount with the same rules, and binds that. The
`pgtoolbox.fyannk.dev` rules are in it only when `console.rbac.operatorKinds` resolves to
true (`auto`: where the cluster serves the operator's kinds), because Kubernetes refuses a
Role that grants verbs its creator does not hold. `make validate-packaging` compares the
Role's rules with the ClusterRole's, so the two cannot drift. When it is
needed, mint a short-lived token and paste it into the form:

```bash
kubectl -n team-a create token pgtoolbox-console-breakglass --duration=1h
```

Every action is audited as that ServiceAccount; revoking it is deleting the binding.
The product stores no password. It is off by default: whoever can read the token holds
dba-level access in the watched namespaces.

## Exposure

`console.exposure.type`: `none` (default: a ClusterIP Service), `ingress`,
`route` (OpenShift) or `httpRoute` (Gateway API). The console streams events over
SSE, so each edge gets a long timeout (`console.exposure.sse.timeout`, default
`1h`): the nginx timeout and buffering annotations on an Ingress, the HAProxy
`timeout` annotation on a Route, `timeouts.request` on an HTTPRoute. Set the
equivalent annotations yourself for any other ingress controller.

**Sticky sessions** (`console.exposure.sticky`, on by default): the edge keeps a
person on one replica with a cookie (`cookieName`, default `pgtoolbox-console-replica`),
so the charts and sparklines they see come from one replica's history. Rendered:
ingress-nginx's `affinity: cookie` (`affinity-mode: persistent`, `Secure` with
Ingress TLS) on the Ingress, Traefik's `service.sticky.cookie` on the Service, the
cookie name on an OpenShift Route (sticky by default; `enabled: false` disables
its cookie). Explicit `exposure.ingress.annotations` win. Gateway API session
persistence is not in the standard channel: configure it on your gateway. For
another controller, set its affinity annotations in `exposure.ingress.annotations`.
Without affinity nothing breaks: the session cookie is self-contained, and
sign-outs and "since" times are shared, so only the charts may differ between
two reloads.

## Metrics

`/metrics` is served in plain HTTP on the probe port, beside `/healthz` and
`/readyz`, and is protected: the caller's token is checked with a
SelfSubjectReview and a SelfSubjectAccessReview for `get /metrics`. Give the scraper's
ServiceAccount that right with `console.metrics.readerClusterRole=true` and
`readerSubjects`, and scrape with `console.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` (it
sends the ServiceAccount token) or a `podMonitor` (which cannot send one; prefer
the ServiceMonitor). With the NetworkPolicy on, list the scraper's namespace in
`networkPolicy.ingress.metricsFrom`.

## The insight pack

`insightPack.enabled` (default `true`) creates the ConfigMap
`<release>-insight-pack` (`insightPack.configMapName`) in each namespace of `insightPack.namespaces` (default:
`console.watchNamespaces`, else the release namespace). It holds CloudNativePG
custom queries for wraparound, vacuum health, blocking, connections,
`pg_stat_statements` and index hygiene, which the console reads from the
instances' exporters: the console itself never connects to PostgreSQL.

Creating it changes nothing. A team opts a Cluster in, without asking anyone,
by adding one line to the Cluster:

```yaml
spec:
  monitoring:
    customQueriesConfigMap: [{name: <release>-insight-pack, key: queries}]
```

The name is per release so that two releases in one namespace do not collide;
the chart tells its console the same name (`INSIGHT_PACK_CONFIGMAP`), which the
console matches against the Cluster and shows in its opt-in line. Set
`insightPack.configMapName: pgtoolbox-insight-pack` to keep the name of
`deploy/insight-pack/insight-pack.yaml`, which the console also expects when
`insightPack.enabled` is `false`.

The ConfigMap carries `cnpg.io/reload`, so a chart upgrade that changes the pack
reloads it on the instances, and its version as the label and annotation
`pgtoolbox.fyannk.dev/insight-pack-version`; the console says when a Cluster
runs an older pack. Without the chart, apply `deploy/insight-pack/insight-pack.yaml`
in the Cluster's namespace. What each query costs and what the screens show:
the documentation's insight pack page.

A team that applies the ConfigMap by hand, or through its own GitOps, owns it:
Helm will not take over a ConfigMap it did not create, and an install or upgrade
fails on it. List those namespaces in `insightPack.skipNamespaces`. A
hand-applied copy is upgraded by hand too, and until it is, the console reports
the Cluster's pack as outdated, still showing what the older pack reports.

## OpenShift

`auth.provider=openshift` makes the console's ServiceAccount the OAuth client: the
chart annotates it `serviceaccounts.openshift.io/oauth-redirecturi.console` with
`console.auth.openshift.redirectURI`, the public callback URL (required; OpenShift
redirects only to URIs the ServiceAccount lists). The client id defaults to the
ServiceAccount's token subject. `PUBLIC_URL` defaults to `https://<exposure.host>`.

The remaining knobs map one to one onto the console's variables:
`auth.openshift.clientID` (`OPENSHIFT_CLIENT_ID`), `clientSecret.existingSecret` (a
Secret mounted as the file `OPENSHIFT_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`; empty means the
ServiceAccount's projected token, which has not yet been verified against a live
OpenShift as a client secret), `discoveryURL` (`OPENSHIFT_DISCOVERY_URL`), `scopes`
(`OPENSHIFT_SCOPES`, default `user:info,user:check-access,user:full`) and
`caConfigMap` (`OPENSHIFT_CA_FILE`). Without `caConfigMap` the chart projects the
`openshift-service-ca.crt` ConfigMap of the namespace next to the API token, which is
where the console looks for the service CA.

## EvidenceAgent channel

The console reads an `EvidenceAgent` (reconciled by the operator) with a
ServiceAccount token the kubelet projects for the audience
`pgtoolbox-evidence-agent/<namespace>`, one per entry of `console.watchNamespaces`
(a token given to an agent in one namespace is refused by the others), at
`/var/run/secrets/pgtoolbox.fyannk.dev/evidence-agent/<namespace>/token`
(`EVIDENCE_TOKEN_DIR` is the directory; `console.evidenceToken`, on by default). The agent validates it with a TokenReview and authorizes it with a
SubjectAccessReview `get evidenceagents/<name>`, which the console Role already
grants. No Secret, no client certificate. The NetworkPolicy selects agent pods by
`app.kubernetes.io/name=evidence-agent` on port 8443, the labels and port the
operator gives every agent; `hack/validate-packaging.sh` compares both with the Go
constants.

## Evidence agents without the operator

`evidence.agents` deploys, for each listed Cluster of the release namespace, the
backup-evidence agent the operator would render for an `EvidenceAgent`: it reads
the Cluster's backup repository and tells the console what it holds (backups, WAL
coverage, the latest scan). Nothing cluster-scoped is rendered and no operator is
needed:

```yaml
evidence:
  agents:
    - cluster: orders
      secrets: [orders-s3]        # every Secret the configuration names
      objectStore: orders-store   # optional: the Role then names it
```

The agent reads barman-cloud repositories, from the plugin's `ObjectStore` or the
Cluster's in-tree `spec.backup.barmanObjectStore`, on:

| Store | Credentials |
|---|---|
| S3 and S3-compatible | a key pair (and session token), or `inheritFromIAMRole`; optionally an endpoint CA, a region from a Secret, and an SSE-C customer key (`sseCustomerKey`) |
| Azure Blob | `connectionString`, `storageAccount` + `storageKey`, `storageAccount` + `storageSasToken`, or `inheritFromAzureAD` / `useDefaultAzureCredentials`; optionally an endpoint CA (Azurite over TLS) |
| GCS | `applicationCredentials`, or `gkeEnvironment`; an `endpointCA` is accepted and not read (barman-cloud uses none for GCS) |

It also reads pgBackRest repositories on S3 and Azure Blob, for a Cluster archiving
with Dalibo's plugin (`pgbackrest.dalibo.com`, a `Stanza`) or Opera's
(`pgbackrest.cnpg.opera.com`, an `Archive`). Name that object in the entry,
`stanza` or `archive` (the Role then names it, and no ObjectStore), and choose the
repository and the endpoint CA under `pgbackrest`:

```yaml
evidence:
  agents:
    - cluster: orders
      secrets: [minio-creds, orders-cipher, minio-ca]
      archive: orders-archive      # or stanza: orders-stanza (Dalibo)
      pgbackrest:
        repository: 1              # repo<n>; Dalibo numbers S3 first, then Azure
        endpointCA: {name: minio-ca, key: ca.crt}  # over the object's own CA
        endpoint: minio.storage.svc:9000           # the pin: the only endpoint
                                                   # the credentials may go to
```

The agent reads one stanza of one repository, with the repository's cipher pass
when it is encrypted. TLS is always verified, whatever the plugin's `verifyTLS` or
`disableVerifyTLS` says: name the CA, or the agent fails on a private one. A
`customEnvVar`, sidecar `env` or extra command argument that moves the repository,
the stanza or the configuration (`PGBACKREST_REPO*`, `PGBACKREST_STANZA`,
`PGBACKREST_CONFIG*`, `--repo*`, `--stanza*`, `--config*`) is refused by name, as is
a `keyType: web-id` or `auto` without `workloadIdentity`.

Every Secret the configuration names, the SSE-C key's and the cipher pass's
included, must be in `secrets`.

**What a Cluster edit can steer.** Whoever may edit the Cluster (or the
ObjectStore) writes the backup configuration the agent follows, which is a wider
set of people than whoever installs the chart. The agent therefore reads only what
its entry allows, and refuses the rest by name (`UnsupportedObjectStore`, shown in
the console):

- only the Secrets in `secrets` (also the Role's only Secret grant);
- two credential settings (access key, secret key, session token, region,
  endpoint CA) may not name the same Secret key;
- an `endpointURL` or emulator destination in plain `http` only with
  `allowInsecureEndpoint: true` (the keys then cross the network in clear text);
- the Pod's cloud identity only with a `workloadIdentity` block;
- with `pgbackrest.endpoint` set (a `host[:port]`), a pgBackRest repository only at
  that endpoint: the S3 endpoint the `Stanza` or `Archive` names, or the Azure
  account's Blob host (`<account>.blob.core.windows.net` host-style). Without the
  pin, whoever edits the `Stanza` or `Archive` chooses where the keys are sent;
- an Azure storage key or SAS token only to the Azure Blob domains (public and
  national clouds), or to the pinned endpoint (Azurite, path-style).

**Workload identity.** With `inheritFromIAMRole`, `inheritFromAzureAD` /
`useDefaultAzureCredentials` or `gkeEnvironment`, list no Secret (the Role then
grants none) and opt in with `workloadIdentity`, which gives the agent's
ServiceAccount its cloud identity:

```yaml
evidence:
  agents:
    - cluster: orders
      workloadIdentity:
        platform: irsa          # gke | eksPodIdentity | irsa | azure
        serviceAccountAnnotations:
          eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/orders-backups   # IRSA
          # azure.workload.identity/client-id: <client id>                           # Azure
          # iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: orders@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com   # GKE
        podLabels:
          azure.workload.identity/use: "true"   # Azure only; quote it
```

The identity needs list and get on the bucket or container. The credential the
agent then uses is explicit, never a default chain:

| Platform | The agent uses |
|---|---|
| `irsa` | the web-identity token the EKS webhook projects (`AWS_ROLE_ARN`, `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`) |
| `eksPodIdentity` | the EKS Pod Identity agent (`AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI` on 169.254.170.23 or fd00:ec2::23, with its token file) |
| `azure` | Azure workload identity (the federated token the Azure webhook projects) |
| `gke` | Application Default Credentials of GKE workload identity |

The node's instance metadata (EC2 IMDS) is never used: the chart sets
`AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` and the agent disables it in code too.
`serviceAccountAnnotations` accepts only `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`,
`eks.amazonaws.com/sts-regional-endpoints`, `eks.amazonaws.com/token-expiration`,
`azure.workload.identity/client-id`, `azure.workload.identity/tenant-id` and
`iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account`; `podLabels` only `azure.workload.identity/use`
(the schema refuses others). `platform` matters with `evidence.networkPolicy`: for
`gke` and `eksPodIdentity` the chart adds, for that agent only, egress to the
metadata endpoint its credentials come from (GKE: 169.254.169.254:80 and
169.254.169.252:988; EKS Pod Identity: 169.254.170.23:80).

A GCS `applicationCredentials` must be a service account key
(`"type": "service_account"`); other credential types (external account,
authorized user) are refused, since they make the agent call endpoints the JSON
names.

Per agent the chart renders a Deployment (one replica, Pod Security
"restricted", no fixed UID, only a projected API token), a Service on port 8443, a
ServiceAccount and a Role + RoleBinding granting exactly:

| Resource | Verbs | Names |
|---|---|---|
| `clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io` | get, list, watch | the agent's Cluster |
| `objectstores.barmancloud.cnpg.io` | get, list, watch | `objectStore`, or any ObjectStore of the namespace when it is empty (they hold references, no secret) |
| `secrets` | **get** only, never list | the entry's `secrets` (no rule at all when it is empty) |

The agent resolves Cluster → barman-cloud configuration → Secrets itself
(`AGENT_RESOLVE=cluster`, the operator's own resolution code), reads the S3 keys
from their Secrets at run time (a rotated key needs no restart), and watches the
Cluster and the ObjectStore by name: when what they resolve to changes it exits and
the kubelet restarts it with the new configuration. Every other Secret value it
was started with (endpoint CA, region, Azure or GCS credential) is re-read every
two minutes with `get` (the Role grants no `watch` on Secrets); a change or a
deletion restarts it the same way. A Secret the configuration names but `secrets`
does not list is never read: the console shows the refusal, naming the Secret and
the value to add.

The console reads these agents from a fixed list (`EVIDENCE_AGENTS_FILE`, the
`<console>-evidence-agents` ConfigMap) and authenticates with a **shared token**:
`evidence.token.existingSecret`, or a Secret `<release>-evidence-token` the chart
generates once (48 random characters) and keeps across upgrades with `lookup`.
`helm template` and client-side GitOps renderers (Argo CD) cannot look it up and
would render a new value on every sync: create the Secret yourself (key `token`,
at least 32 characters) and name it. Both sides re-read the file, so a rotation
needs no restart.

`evidence.tls.mode` says how the console reaches the agents:

| Mode | Transport | The console trusts |
|---|---|---|
| `none` (default) | plain HTTP inside the namespace; the shared token crosses the pod network in clear text | nothing to verify |
| `certManager` | HTTPS, a Certificate per agent from `evidence.tls.certManager.issuerRef` | each agent's `ca.crt` (an issuer that fills it, such as a CA issuer) |
| `openshiftServiceCA` | HTTPS, the Service's serving certificate from the OpenShift service CA | the `openshift-service-ca.crt` ConfigMap |

`evidence.networkPolicy.enabled` (off by default, like the console's) isolates the
agent pods: ingress from this release's console pods on port 8443 only; egress to
DNS, the API server (the same `addresses`/`any` rule as the console's) and the
object store (`evidence.networkPolicy.objectStore.to` peers, or any address on its
`ports`). The console's own policy already admits the agents (same labels and
port as the operator's).

**Limits, compared with the operator's `EvidenceAgent`:**

- a Cluster created later gets no agent until it is listed here;
- the Secrets the configuration names must be listed by hand (`secrets`);
- pgBackRest repositories through Dalibo's or Opera's plugin only, and one
  stanza of one repository per agent;
- the agents live in the release namespace only, which the console must watch;
- there is no `EvidenceAgent` status: the console compares no `producerEpoch`
  and shows the agent under its Cluster's name;
- with `tls.mode: none` the token is sent in clear text inside the cluster
  network: prefer a TLS mode, or enable the NetworkPolicy.

## NetworkPolicy: the installing admin's choice, never on by default

`console.networkPolicy.enabled` is `false`, and that is deliberate: whether the
cluster enforces policies, and whether this namespace wants one, is known only to
whoever installs the chart. A default-deny rendered unasked breaks exposure, DNS
or the API-server path the moment the list misses something. **RBAC and
SubjectAccessReview are the isolation the product guarantees**; the policy is an
extra network boundary. Two limits, stated plainly:

1. **Enforcement is a property of the CNI.** The chart cannot prove the cluster
   enforces NetworkPolicy; on a CNI that does not, the object is accepted and
   does nothing.
2. **It is derived from `watchNamespaces`, never from a request**, and lists the
   console's real egress only: the watched Clusters' instance pods
   (`:8000` status, `:9187` metrics), their poolers (`:9127`), the EvidenceAgent
   pods, the API server and DNS; ingress only from the routers (the
   `policy-group.network.openshift.io/ingress` namespaces for a Route,
   `console.exposure.routerNamespace` otherwise) and
   `networkPolicy.ingress.extraFrom`, on the console port. With nothing
   exposed and no extra peer, no ingress is admitted at all.

The API-server egress uses the addresses of the `kubernetes` EndpointSlice, looked up
at install time. Where the lookup is not possible (`helm template`, `--dry-run`)
the chart **fails** rather than guess; set `networkPolicy.apiServer.addresses`,
or `mode: any` (any address on 443/6443), the documented fallback for API servers
behind a load balancer. On OpenShift set `networkPolicy.dns` to the
`openshift-dns` namespace and port `5353`.

The kind e2e (`make test-e2e-chart-netpol`) exercises the enabled policy on Calico
as an additional check, after a canary proving the CNI really enforces.

## The console binary contract

The chart sets these environment variables; the console binary reads them
(`internal/console/config`): `WATCH_NAMESPACES`, `CLUSTER_SELECTOR`, `LISTEN_ADDR`,
`PROBE_LISTEN_ADDR`, `AUTH_PROVIDER`, `SESSION_KEY_FILE`, `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`,
`OIDC_*` (issuer, client id/secret file, redirect URL, scopes, `OIDC_CA_FILE`,
`OIDC_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFIED` when false, `OIDC_GRANT_CLIENT_ID` and
`OIDC_GRANT_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE` with `oidc.grantClient`), `PUBLIC_URL`, `SESSION_MAX_AGE`,
`AUTH_TOKEN_LOGIN` when false, `IDP_TIMEOUT`, `COOKIE_SECURE`,
`TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, `TLS_CERT_FILE`/`TLS_KEY_FILE`, `REVOCATION_CONFIGMAP`, `INSIGHT_PACK_CONFIGMAP`, `INSTANCE_STATUS_CA_FILE`,
`ALLOW_CLUSTER_CATALOGS`, `ALLOW_LOGS`, `LOG_STREAM_ENABLED`, `LOG_MATCH_MAX_AGE`, `EVIDENCE_ENABLED` when false, `EVIDENCE_TOKEN_DIR`, `EVIDENCE_AGENTS_FILE`, `EVIDENCE_INTERVAL`, `OPERATIONS_ENABLED` when false, `RESTORE_DRILL_*` with `restoreDrills.enabled`, `MONITORING_URL`, `PROMETHEUS_URL`, `PROMETHEUS_TOKEN_FILE`, `PROMETHEUS_CA_FILE`, `PROMETHEUS_NAMESPACED`, `PROMETHEUS_RANGE`, `HISTORY_ENABLED`, `HISTORY_PATH`,
`POD_NAMESPACE`, and with `auth.provider=openshift` `OPENSHIFT_CLIENT_ID`,
`OPENSHIFT_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`, `OPENSHIFT_DISCOVERY_URL`, `OPENSHIFT_SCOPES` and
`OPENSHIFT_CA_FILE` (internal/console/auth). `OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` is gone: groups come
from the API server. `hack/validate-packaging.sh` fails when the chart renders a
variable the binary does not read. `console.extraEnv` appends more.

The evidence agents (`evidence.agents`) get `RUNTIME_MODE=agent`, `LISTEN_ADDR`,
`AGENT_NAME`, `AGENT_NAMESPACE`, `AGENT_AUTH=sharedtoken`, `AGENT_TOKEN_FILE`,
`AGENT_RESOLVE=cluster`, `CNPG_CLUSTER_NAME`, `AGENT_ALLOWED_SECRETS`, then
`AGENT_PLAIN_HTTP=true` or `TLS_CERT_FILE`/`TLS_KEY_FILE`, and `LOG_LEVEL`
(internal/evidence/config); `hack/validate-packaging.sh` checks the agent binary
reads each of them.

make helm-lint helm-unittest chart-lint chart-kubeconform chart-kube-linter validate-packaging

## pgAdmin without the operator

`pgadmin.enabled: true` (off by default) installs one pgAdmin for the team, in
the release namespace, with nothing cluster-scoped. The operator's
`PgAdmin` works the Clusters out by itself; this chart does not: the servers are
**declared** in `pgadmin.servers`, and every server says where its credential
comes from. There is no default: an implicit `none` would look like a broken
setup, an implicit Secret would be a guess.

```yaml
pgadmin:
  enabled: true
  auth:
    provider: oidc            # or openshift (an oauth-proxy, exposure.type route)
    oidc:
      issuerURL: https://idp.example.com/realms/corp
      clientID: pgadmin
      clientSecret: {existingSecret: pgadmin-oidc}
  admins: [alice@example.com]
  servers:
    - cluster: orders
      endpoint: rw                      # rw | ro | r | pooler:<name>
      credentials:
        application: {secret: orders-app}
    - cluster: orders
      endpoint: ro
      credentials:
        databaseRole: {name: orders-reporting, secret: orders-reporting-password}
    - cluster: billing
      endpoint: rw
      database: billing
      user: billing_owner
      credentials: {secret: billing-owner}   # yours: basic-auth, or a pgpass key
    - cluster: legacy
      endpoint: rw
      database: app
      user: alice
      credentials: none                       # pgAdmin asks for the password
```

An `ro` server needs a replica. CloudNativePG's `<cluster>-ro` Service routes to
the replicas only: on a Cluster of one instance (`spec.instances: 1`) it has no
endpoints and pgAdmin gets `Connection refused`; a Cluster that lists `ro` or `r`
in `spec.managed.services.disabledDefaultServices` has no such Service at all.
The chart applies the operator's rule: the `passfile-sync` sidecar, which watches
the Clusters the values name, withholds such a server, and the `registration`
sidecar leaves it out of pgAdmin. Both log the server's name and the reason
(`no replica: the Cluster has one instance`, `the Cluster disabled its ro
Service`). The rule reads the Cluster's spec, not its readiness, so a replica
that restarts does not make the server come and go. Scale the Cluster to two
instances (or enable the Service) and the server is registered within seconds,
without a Pod restart; back to one instance, it is removed. The console's
topology view shows an `ro` Service with no replica behind it.

### What you give up next to the operator

| | Operator (`PgAdmin`) | This chart |
|---|---|---|
| New Cluster or DatabaseRole | Registered automatically | Add it to `pgadmin.servers`, `helm upgrade` |
| Which Secret holds which credential | Worked out from the Cluster | Named by you, checked live |
| DatabaseRole password before CloudNativePG applied it | Never offered | Never offered (the sidecar checks) |
| Password rotation | Automatic | Automatic |
| Clusters of other namespaces | With a grant in that namespace | No |
| Status in the console | Conditions per server | Sidecar logs only |
| Settings database | CloudNativePG `Database` | SQLite on a PVC; or a PostgreSQL database you create, its URI in a Secret you name (`pgadmin.configDatabase.existingSecret`) |
| Backup before a pgAdmin upgrade | Job | Init container, local copy; none with `configDatabase` (back the database up where it lives) |

### Only the Secrets you name

The Pod's Role grants `get` and `watch` on exactly the Clusters, DatabaseRoles,
Poolers and Secrets `pgadmin.servers` names, by `resourceNames`: each server's
credential Secret and, unless it names a `caConfigMap`, its CA Secret. No
`list`, no other Secret of the namespace, nothing cluster-scoped. The sidecar
watches each object by name (a field selector on `metadata.name`, which the API
server authorizes against `resourceNames`), so a rotated password reaches
pgAdmin within seconds.

### The server CA: `caConfigMap` or `caSecret`

libpq verifies each server (`verify-full`) against the Cluster's server CA,
which a server takes from one of:

| Field | What the Pod reads | Checked against the Cluster |
|---|---|---|
| `caConfigMap: <name>` (preferred) | a ConfigMap holding only `ca.crt`, mounted into `passfile-sync` (projected, optional); the Role names no CA Secret | no: the Pod may not read the CA Secret, `verify-full` decides |
| `caSecret: <name>` | that Secret's `ca.crt`, by `get` and `watch` | yes: it must be `spec.certificates.serverCASecret`, else `<cluster>-ca` |
| neither (**deprecated**) | the derived `<cluster>-ca`, by `get` and `watch` | yes |

The two fields are exclusive (the schema refuses both on one server), and every
server of one Cluster names the same `caConfigMap`: the Pod keeps one CA file per
Cluster.

The derived default goes against "the sidecar reads only the Secrets named in
values": `<cluster>-ca` is not named, and the Secret CloudNativePG generates under
that name also holds `ca.key`, the CA's signing key. The sidecar copies only
`ca.crt`, but the Role lets the Pod read the key. This minor keeps the default
and `helm install`/`upgrade` prints a NOTES warning naming each Secret granted
that way; **the next minor requires `caSecret` or `caConfigMap` on every
server.** To move to a ConfigMap:

```bash
kubectl -n <ns> get secret <cluster>-ca -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d > ca.crt
kubectl -n <ns> create configmap <cluster>-ca-crt --from-file=ca.crt=ca.crt
```

then set `caConfigMap: <cluster>-ca-crt` on every server of that Cluster. The
kubelet keeps the mounted file current and `passfile-sync` follows it without a
restart, but a copy made once does not follow CloudNativePG's CA renewal (every
90 days by default): keep the ConfigMap current with trust-manager, or give the
Cluster one long-lived `serverCASecret`. Until the ConfigMap exists its servers
have no service section, and the sidecar's log says why.

Before it uses a named Secret, the sidecar checks it against live state, by the
operator's own rules (`internal/operator/cnpgcred`):

- `application`: the Cluster must designate that Secret (`<cluster>-app`, or the
  `secret` its `recovery`, `pg_basebackup` or `initdb` bootstrap names); the user
  and database come from the Cluster.
- `superuser`: only with `enableSuperuserAccess: true`, and the Secret must be
  `<cluster>-superuser` or `spec.superuserSecret`; user and database `postgres`.
- `databaseRole`: the DatabaseRole must name that Secret as its password
  Secret, and CloudNativePG must report the role applied at its current
  generation, with that Secret at the version it applied.
- `secret` and `none`: nothing to check against; `user` and `database` are
  required.
- `caSecret` (or the derived `<cluster>-ca`) must be the Cluster's server CA
  (`spec.certificates.serverCASecret`, else `<cluster>-ca`); a `caConfigMap` is
  not checked; a Pooler endpoint must belong to the Cluster.

A mismatch (the Cluster was recreated with another bootstrap, the role now
points elsewhere, the role is not applied yet) is never used: the server stays
listed, pgAdmin asks for the password, and the sidecar logs the server's name
and the reason, never a value:

```bash
kubectl -n <ns> logs deploy/<release>-pgadmin -c passfile-sync
```

### Which Secret CloudNativePG creates

| Cluster | Application Secret | `credentials` to declare |
|---|---|---|
| `bootstrap.initdb` (also the default: CloudNativePG sets owner and database `app`) | `<cluster>-app`, user = `initdb.owner`, database = `initdb.database` | `application: {secret: <cluster>-app}` |
| `bootstrap.initdb.secret.name` set | that Secret (yours); no `<cluster>-app` | `application: {secret: <that name>}` |
| `bootstrap.recovery` / `pg_basebackup` with `owner` and `database` | `<cluster>-app` | `application: {secret: <cluster>-app}` |
| `bootstrap.recovery` / `pg_basebackup` with `.secret.name` | that Secret (yours) | `application: {secret: <that name>}` |
| `bootstrap.recovery` / `pg_basebackup` without `owner` and `database`, or a replica Cluster | none | `secret: <yours>` or `none`, with `user` and `database` |
| `enableSuperuserAccess: true` | `<cluster>-superuser`, or `spec.superuserSecret` | `superuser: {secret: <cluster>-superuser}` |
| `enableSuperuserAccess` unset or false | none usable | `superuser` is refused |
| A `DatabaseRole` with `passwordSecret` | that Secret | `databaseRole: {name: <role>, secret: <that name>}` |

### Registration, upgrades and storage

- At every Pod start the `registration` native sidecar writes the declared list
  into pgAdmin's "PgToolBox" group (`setup.py dump-servers` → keep everything
  outside the group → `load-servers`) once pgAdmin has created its settings
  database; servers people added themselves are kept. It leaves out the servers
  `passfile-sync` withholds (an `ro` or `r` endpoint the Cluster cannot serve,
  above), which it reads from a file on an `emptyDir` the two share (names and
  reasons only; the registration has no API token), and registers again when
  that file changes. The list is a ConfigMap
  whose checksum is on the Pod template: a `helm upgrade` that changes it rolls
  the Pod. No Helm hook Job: a second Pod cannot open SQLite on the
  ReadWriteOnce volume.
- Before the first start of a new pgAdmin image, the `pre-upgrade-backup` init
  container copies the settings database aside (SQLite's online backup) into
  `.pgtoolbox/backups` on the same PVC and keeps `pgadmin.backups.keep` copies.
- One replica, `Recreate`. The PVC is kept on `helm uninstall`
  (`pgadmin.storage.keep`).
- Sign-in is `oidc` (pgAdmin's OAuth2 client) or `openshift` (an oauth-proxy;
  by default whoever may `get secrets` in the namespace gets in, see
  `pgadmin.auth.openshift.sar`). There is no local password login.
- `console.pgadmin.url` gives the console a fixed pgAdmin link: no `PgAdmin`
  object announces this one.
- `pgadmin.networkPolicy.enabled` (off by default) renders exactly pgAdmin's
  egress (DNS, the declared Clusters' and Poolers' pods on 5432, the API
  server, the identity provider on 443) and ingress from the router namespace.

## Values reference

Every value, with its default and what it does. The table is generated from the
`# --` comments of `values.yaml` (the same file `helm show values` prints) and
`make chart-docs-check` fails when it is stale. `values.schema.json` is the
authority on what is accepted.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| global.imageRegistry | string | `""` | Registry that prefixes every image of the chart, for an air-gapped install that mirrors the product images (`registry.corp:5000/mirror`). Empty leaves the references as written. |
| commonLabels | object | `{}` | Labels added to every resource. |
| console.enabled | bool | `true` | Install the console. `false` renders only the other sections (the evidence agents, pgAdmin, the insight pack). |
| console.fullnameOverride | string | `""` | Name of the console's objects. Default: the release name when it already says "console", otherwise `<release>-console`. |
| console.image.repository | string | `"ghcr.io/fyannk/pgtoolbox-console"` | Repository of the console image. |
| console.image.tag | string | `""` | Tag of the console image. Empty: the chart's `appVersion`. |
| console.image.digest | string | `""` | Digest of the console image (`sha256:...`). It wins over the tag; air-gapped installs pin by it. |
| console.image.pullPolicy | string | `"IfNotPresent"` | Pull policy of the console image. |
| console.imagePullSecrets | list | `[]` | Pull Secrets for the image, as `[{name: regcred}]`. |
| console.watchNamespaces | list | `[]` | Namespaces the console watches and receives a Role in. Empty: the release namespace. A short list the team owns (the schema allows 16); the console refuses to start with none and never watches all namespaces. |
| console.clusterSelector | object | `{}` | Labels a Cluster must all carry to be shown, on top of what each user's own RBAC allows. |
| console.replicas | int | `2` | Console replicas, with in-memory or persistent history. Each replica keeps its own history; `exposure.sticky` keeps a person on one. |
| console.history.persistent | bool | `false` | Keep the history (and the state snapshots, the timeline, the digests) on a volume per replica: the console is then a StatefulSet with one claim per replica, `history-<console>-<ordinal>`, rolling one pod at a time. `false`: history in memory, a Deployment. Off by default because a team namespace may have no StorageClass; turn it on where one exists. Coming from chart 1.2, read the README ("Persistent history") first. |
| console.history.size | string | `"1Gi"` | Size of each replica's history claim. 1Gi holds the default retention with room: see the README for the sizing. A StatefulSet's claim template cannot change: a new size applies to claims made later. |
| console.history.storageClassName | string | `""` | StorageClass of the history claims. Empty: the cluster's default. |
| console.digest.enabled | string | `nil` | Serve the daily digest page. `null`: on with `history.persistent`. With in-memory history each replica would build its own digest and lose it on restart, so set `true` to have the page anyway (it then differs per replica). |
| console.digest.hour | string | `nil` | UTC hour (0-23) at which each digest closes its 24 hours. `null`: 7. |
| console.digest.retention | string | `""` | How long digests are kept, a Go duration between 24h and 8784h. Empty: 720h. |
| console.digest.delivery.timeout | string | `""` | Bound of one delivery attempt (1s to 1m). Empty: 10s. Failed attempts are retried with backoff and shown on the admin page; they never block anything else. |
| console.digest.delivery.chat | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"url"}` | Slack or Mattermost incoming-webhook URL (https), read from a key of a Secret you create: `{existingSecret: name, key: url}`. |
| console.digest.delivery.webhook | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"url"}` | Generic webhook URL (https) that receives the digest's JSON summary, read from a key of a Secret you create: `{existingSecret: name, key: url}`. |
| console.digest.delivery.smtp.address | string | `""` | SMTP server as `host:port`. Empty: mail delivery is off. |
| console.digest.delivery.smtp.tls | string | `"starttls"` | `starttls` (required, never optional) or `tls` (implicit, port 465). There is no plaintext mode. |
| console.digest.delivery.smtp.username | string | `""` | SMTP user name (AUTH PLAIN, over TLS only). |
| console.digest.delivery.smtp.password | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"password"}` | SMTP password, read from a key of a Secret you create: `{existingSecret: name, key: password}`. |
| console.digest.delivery.smtp.from | string | `""` | Sender address of the digest mail. |
| console.digest.delivery.smtp.to | list | `[]` | Recipient addresses of the digest mail. |
| console.auth.provider | string | `"token"` | How people sign in. `token`: paste an API server token (break-glass; works everywhere). `oidc`: code flow against an IdP the API server also trusts, so the token is an API server token. `openshift`: the OpenShift OAuth code flow. |
| console.auth.oidc.issuerURL | string | `""` | Issuer URL of the OIDC provider. |
| console.auth.oidc.clientID | string | `""` | OIDC client ID. |
| console.auth.oidc.clientSecret | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"client-secret"}` | OIDC client secret, read from a Secret you create and mounted as a file: `{existingSecret: name, key: client-secret}`. |
| console.auth.oidc.redirectURL | string | `""` | Callback URL registered with the IdP. Empty: derived from `publicURL`. |
| console.auth.oidc.scopes | list | `["openid","email","profile","offline_access"]` | OIDC scopes requested at sign-in. |
| console.auth.oidc.caConfigMap | string | `""` | ConfigMap with a PEM bundle (key `ca.crt`) that trusts a private IdP, mounted as `OIDC_CA_FILE`. Empty: the system roots. |
| console.auth.oidc.requireEmailVerified | bool | `true` | Refuse a login whose ID token does not carry `email_verified=true`. Set `false` only for an IdP that omits the claim. |
| console.auth.oidc.grantClient.clientID | string | `""` | OIDC client ID of grant sign-ins. Empty: off. |
| console.auth.oidc.grantClient.clientSecret | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"client-secret"}` | Its client secret, from a Secret you create: `{existingSecret: name, key: client-secret}`. |
| console.auth.openshift.redirectURI | string | `""` | Public callback URL of the console. Required: it becomes the `serviceaccounts.openshift.io/oauth-redirecturi.console` annotation of the console's ServiceAccount, which is the OAuth client, and OpenShift only redirects to URIs the ServiceAccount lists. |
| console.auth.openshift.clientID | string | `""` | OAuth client ID (`OPENSHIFT_CLIENT_ID`). Empty: read from the console's projected token (`system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<serviceaccount>`). |
| console.auth.openshift.clientSecret | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"token"}` | Secret holding a long-lived ServiceAccount token to present as the client secret (`OPENSHIFT_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`). Empty: the console presents its projected ServiceAccount token. Whether OpenShift accepts a bound projected token there is not yet verified on a live cluster; if it does not, create the token Secret and name it here. |
| console.auth.openshift.discoveryURL | string | `""` | Metadata document of the OAuth server (`OPENSHIFT_DISCOVERY_URL`, https only). Empty: `https://openshift.default.svc/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. |
| console.auth.openshift.scopes | list | `["user:info","user:check-access","user:full"]` | OAuth scopes requested (`OPENSHIFT_SCOPES`). Narrow the defaults only knowingly. |
| console.auth.openshift.caConfigMap | string | `""` | ConfigMap with `ca.crt` that trusts the OAuth server (`OPENSHIFT_CA_FILE`). Empty: the service CA OpenShift mounts into every pod. |
| console.auth.sessionKey | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"session-key"}` | Secret holding the key that seals the session cookie (AES-GCM under HKDF keys). Empty `existingSecret`: the chart generates 32 random bytes once and keeps them across upgrades; all replicas share them, so a login survives a roll. |
| console.auth.sessionIdleTimeout | string | `"1h"` | Idle timeout of a session. It must not exceed `sessionMaxAge`. |
| console.auth.sessionMaxAge | string | `""` | Maximum age of a session whatever its activity. Empty: the console's default, 12h. |
| console.auth.tokenLogin | bool | `true` | Show the break-glass form (paste an API server token) next to single sign-on. `false` removes the form. |
| console.auth.idpTimeout | string | `""` | Time limit of calls to the IdP or OAuth server. Empty: the console's default. |
| console.breakGlass.enabled | bool | `false` | Render the break-glass ServiceAccount (it automounts nothing and holds no token) and, in each watched namespace, a RoleBinding to the `pgtoolbox-console-operator` ClusterRole, which must exist. Mint a short-lived token when needed and paste it into the login form. |
| console.breakGlass.serviceAccountName | string | `"pgtoolbox-console-breakglass"` | Name of the break-glass ServiceAccount. |
| console.breakGlass.roleKind | string | `"ClusterRole"` | What the RoleBinding points at. `ClusterRole` binds the `pgtoolbox-console-operator` ClusterRole, which the pgtoolbox chart (`operator.userRoles.create`) or `config/rbac` must have created. `Role` renders, in each watched namespace, a Role of the same rules (the `pgtoolbox.fyannk.dev` ones only when `console.rbac.operatorKinds` resolves to true) and binds that: for a namespace admin who installs without the operator. |
| console.publicURL | string | `""` | URL people type, `https://host/`. Used for cookies, redirects and the OpenShift callback. Default: `https://<exposure.host>` when a host is set. |
| console.cookieSecure | string | `""` | Force the session cookie's `Secure` attribute (`true` or `false`). Empty keeps the console's rule: Secure unless the request is plain loopback HTTP. |
| console.trustedProxyHops | int | `nil` | Reverse-proxy hops to trust for `X-Forwarded-For`, 0 to 8. 0 trusts none. Empty: 1 when `exposure.type` is not `none` (the Ingress, Route or gateway in front), 0 otherwise. Set it explicitly when more proxies sit in front (a CDN, a load balancer that appends to the header) or none does. The header is read only from the peers of `trustedProxyCIDRs`. |
| console.trustedProxyCIDRs | list | `[]` | Addresses (CIDRs) of the reverse proxies in front, as the console sees them: the ingress controller or router Pods, the nodes for a host-network router. The console reads `X-Forwarded-For` only from a peer inside one, so that a Pod calling the Service directly cannot name a new address on every request and escape the per-address sign-in budgets. Empty: every peer when `networkPolicy.enabled`, an exposure is set, `networkPolicy.ingress.extraFrom` is empty (the policy then admits only the router namespace) and the cluster is not OpenShift (no Route API, no `route` exposure: its project template adds `allow-from-same-namespace`); otherwise none, and the header is ignored: every client then shares the proxy's address, so no per-address budget applies, only the per-flow, per-token and per-replica bounds (the console warns at start, NOTES at install). NetworkPolicies add up and the chart cannot see the others: one that admits more Pods to the console port (an `allow-same-namespace`) lets them forge the header under the any-peer trust. List the proxies here where such a policy exists, and on OpenShift. |
| console.platform | string | `"auto"` | Platform the chart renders for: `auto` (detect OpenShift from the API server: `route.openshift.io/v1`), `kubernetes` or `openshift`. `openshift` keeps the console from trusting `X-Forwarded-For` from every peer (see `trustedProxyCIDRs`). Set it with a client-side `helm template` or `helm install --dry-run=client`, which have no API server to ask: the chart then sees no Route API even for OpenShift, unless you pass `--api-versions route.openshift.io/v1`. A `route` exposure always counts as OpenShift. |
| console.tls.secretName | string | `""` | kubernetes.io/tls Secret that makes the console serve HTTPS on `port` (mounted as files). Point the edge at it with your controller's backend-protocol setting. |
| console.evidence.enabled | bool | `true` | Read repository evidence from the namespace's EvidenceAgents (`EVIDENCE_ENABLED`). Off, the backups screen says "disabled" instead of looking for an agent. |
| console.evidence.interval | string | `""` | How often each agent is asked again (`EVIDENCE_INTERVAL`). Empty keeps the console's default. |
| console.operations.enabled | bool | `true` | Serve the operations endpoints (backup, reload, restart, promote; `OPERATIONS_ENABLED`). Every write is still made with the caller's own token and authorized by the API server. `false` makes the endpoints answer 501. |
| console.mcp.enabled | bool | `false` | Serve the read-only MCP endpoint at `/mcp` (`MCP_ENABLED`) and the console's OAuth authorization server for MCP clients. Bearer tokens only; every tool runs as the token's owner. Requires a public URL. |
| console.mcp.writeTools | bool | `false` | Add the MCP write tools `backup`, `reload`, `restart`, `promote` (`MCP_WRITE_TOOLS`). Requires `mcp.enabled` and `operations.enabled`. Each runs as the person, once confirmed: backup and reload in the client's form, restart and promote on a console page (URL elicitation). |
| console.mcp.maxResultBytes | int | `nil` | Cap on one tool result's JSON in bytes (`MCP_MAX_RESULT_BYTES`), 16384 to 4194304; a larger result is shortened and says so. `null`: the console's default, 262144 (256 KiB). |
| console.mcp.callTimeout | string | `""` | Time limit of one tool call (`MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT`), a Go duration from `1s` to `50s`. Empty: the console's default, `20s`. |
| console.mcp.oauthAccessTTL | string | `""` | Lifetime of an access token the console issues to an MCP client (`MCP_OAUTH_ACCESS_TTL`), from `10s` to `1h`; the client renews it with its refresh token. Empty: the console's default, `1h`. |
| console.mcp.oauthClientMetadataDocuments | bool | `false` | Accept OAuth client ID metadata documents (`MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_METADATA_DOCUMENTS`): a client names itself with an HTTPS URL and the console fetches the document there, from public addresses only (and only from `oauthClientMetadataHosts` when set). The console then needs HTTPS (TCP 443) to the Internet: with `networkPolicy.enabled`, allow it in `networkPolicy.extraEgress`. Dynamic registration, always on, needs no egress. |
| console.mcp.oauthClientMetadataHosts | list | `[]` | The only hosts (DNS names) client ID metadata documents are fetched from (`MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_METADATA_HOSTS`), for example `[claude.ai, chatgpt.com]`; applies with `oauthClientMetadataDocuments`. Empty: any public address. |
| console.tracing.endpoint | string | `""` | OTLP/HTTP base URL (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`); `/v1/traces` is appended. Empty: tracing is off. For example `http://jaeger-collector.monitoring:4318` or `https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel`. |
| console.tracing.headersSecret | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"headers"}` | Exporter headers (an API key, a project name), read from a key of a Secret you create, `key=value,...` (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` format), mounted as a file (`TRACING_HEADERS_FILE`): `{existingSecret: name, key: headers}`. |
| console.tracing.serviceName | string | `""` | Service name (`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`). Empty: `pgtoolbox-console`. |
| console.tracing.sampler | string | `""` | Sampler (`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`): `parentbased_always_on` (the default), `parentbased_traceidratio`, `traceidratio`, `always_on`, `always_off`, `parentbased_always_off`. |
| console.tracing.samplerArg | string | `""` | Ratio of the traceidratio samplers (`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`), `"0"` to `"1"`. |
| console.tracing.includePayloads | bool | `false` | Add MCP tool arguments and results to the tool spans, redacted and capped at 16 KiB each (`TRACING_INCLUDE_PAYLOADS`). Tokens never. |
| console.restoreDrills.enabled | bool | `false` | Enable the "Run a restore drill" operation of the Backups screen. Adds a Role in the drill namespace(s) that can get, list, watch and delete Clusters. Requires `operations.enabled`. |
| console.restoreDrills.namespace | string | `""` | Namespace where drill Clusters run. Empty: each source Cluster's own namespace. It must be a watched namespace. A dedicated drill namespace is strongly recommended. |
| console.restoreDrills.prefix | string | `"drill-"` | Name prefix of the drill Clusters (at most 20 characters). |
| console.restoreDrills.timeLimit | string | `"2h"` | How long an unfinished drill runs before it is recorded as timed out and deleted. |
| console.restoreDrills.maxConcurrent | int | `3` | Drills of this console running at once (1 to 20). |
| console.restoreDrills.resources | object | `{"limits":{"cpu":"","memory":""},"requests":{"cpu":"","memory":""}}` | Resource requests and limits of the drill instance. Empty values keep the source Cluster's. |
| console.restoreDrills.storage | object | `{"size":"","storageClass":""}` | Storage of the drill instance: `size` and `storageClass`. Empty values keep the source Cluster's. |
| console.restoreDrills.serverCA.mode | string | `"auto"` | CA that signs each drill's server certificate: `auto`, `source`, `secret` or `own` (see the comment above). |
| console.restoreDrills.serverCA.secret | string | `""` | CA Secret (`ca.crt` and `ca.key`) in every drill namespace, for mode `secret` (and `auto`); its `ca.crt` must be in `instanceStatus.caBundleConfigMap`. |
| console.restoreDrills.sealKey | object | `{"existingSecret":"","key":"keys"}` | The drill seal's own keys, mounted as a file (`RESTORE_DRILL_SEAL_KEY_FILE`): `{existingSecret: name, key: keys}`. Empty `existingSecret`: the keys derive from the session secret. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.enabled | bool | `true` | Render the drill Pods' NetworkPolicy in every drill namespace. On with drills: a promoted drill is a live copy of a production database, and extensions the console cannot neutralise must not reach the network. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.apiServer.mode | string | `"any"` | How egress to the API server is allowed: `any` (any address on `apiServer.ports`, so that the policy renders without a cluster) or `addresses` (only `apiServer.addresses`). |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.apiServer.addresses | list | `[]` | API server IP addresses to allow when `apiServer.mode` is `addresses` and the EndpointSlice lookup is unavailable (`helm template`, GitOps renderers). |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.apiServer.ports | list | `[443,6443]` | Ports of the API server that egress is allowed to. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.dns.namespace | string | `"kube-system"` | Namespace of the cluster DNS pods that egress is allowed to. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.dns.podLabels | object | `{"k8s-app":"kube-dns"}` | Labels that select the cluster DNS pods. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.dns.ports | list | `[53]` | Ports of the cluster DNS pods (TCP and UDP). OpenShift DNS pods listen on 5353: use `[5353]` there. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.objectStore.to | list | `[]` | Where the object store is, as raw NetworkPolicy `to` peers (an `ipBlock`, or a `namespaceSelector` for an in-cluster MinIO). Empty allows any address on `objectStore.ports`. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.objectStore.ports | list | `[443]` | Ports of the object store that egress is allowed to. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.operator.namespace | string | `"cnpg-system"` | Namespace of the CloudNativePG operator, which reaches every instance's status port. |
| console.restoreDrills.networkPolicy.operator.podLabels | object | `{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"cloudnative-pg"}` | Labels that select the CloudNativePG operator pods. |
| console.restoreDrills.admissionPolicy.create | bool | `false` | Render a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (Kubernetes 1.30 or newer) that lets the console delete only Clusters carrying its drill-owner label, its seal annotation and the drill prefix. Cluster-scoped, so a cluster admin sets it (or applies the rendered policy). |
| console.restoreDrills.admissionPolicy.validationActions | list | `["Deny"]` | Validation actions of the binding: `Deny`, `Warn` and/or `Audit`. Only `Deny` blocks a request. |
| console.monitoringURL | string | `""` | Link-out to the site's monitoring system (`MONITORING_URL`): https, or root-relative. Empty: no link. |
| console.pgadmin.url | string | `""` | Fixed pgAdmin link shown on every Cluster (`PGADMIN_URL`): https, or root-relative. For a pgAdmin without the operator, which no PgAdmin object announces. Empty: the console links only the PgAdmin objects that register a Cluster. |
| console.prometheus.url | string | `""` | Prometheus HTTP API the console queries for its metrics charts (`PROMETHEUS_URL`): on OpenShift `https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc:9091` (with `namespaced: true`, the tenancy port). Empty: the charts come from the console's own ring. http is accepted only without a token. |
| console.prometheus.token.secret | object | `{"key":"token","name":""}` | Secret key holding a bearer token for the queries (https only), mounted as a file: `{name, key}`. |
| console.prometheus.token.projected | object | `{"enabled":false,"expirationSeconds":3600}` | Use the console's own ServiceAccount token instead, which the kubelet rotates in place (what the OpenShift thanos-querier accepts once the ServiceAccount may view metrics): `{enabled, expirationSeconds}`. |
| console.prometheus.caConfigMap | string | `""` | ConfigMap with `ca.crt` that signed the server certificate (OpenShift: `openshift-service-ca.crt`, copied into the namespace). Empty: the system roots. |
| console.prometheus.namespaced | bool | `false` | Add `namespace=<ns>` to each query (`PROMETHEUS_NAMESPACED`), as OpenShift's tenancy port requires. |
| console.prometheus.range | string | `""` | Window of the charts (`PROMETHEUS_RANGE`, 5m to 24h). Empty: the console's 1h. |
| console.evidenceToken.enabled | bool | `true` | Authenticate to the EvidenceAgents with a projected ServiceAccount token (no Secret), one per watched namespace, with the audience `pgtoolbox-evidence-agent/<namespace>`. The agent checks it with a TokenReview and a SubjectAccessReview. |
| console.evidenceToken.expirationSeconds | int | `3600` | Lifetime of the projected token, rotated in place by the kubelet. |
| console.instanceStatus.caBundleConfigMap | string | `"pgtoolbox-console-instance-ca"` | ConfigMap with the key `ca.crt` that you supply, holding the PEM server CAs of the watched Clusters. The console verifies each instance's `/pg/status` against it; a Cluster missing from the bundle is shown as "not verifiable". Empty disables the mount. Create it with the command in the README. |
| console.revocations.configMapName | string | `""` | Name of the revocation ConfigMap, which every replica watches so that a revoked session dies everywhere. The chart creates it empty; an admin edits its keys `notBefore`, `users` and `sessions`. Empty: `<fullname>-revocations`. |
| console.lifecycle.configMapName | string | `""` | Name of a ConfigMap you manage (key `lifecycle.json`) with the end-of-life table the diagnostics read. Empty: the chart creates `<fullname>-lifecycle` from the table this chart version ships and refreshes it on every upgrade. |
| console.clusterImageCatalogs.enabled | bool | `false` | Read ClusterImageCatalog objects (a cluster-scoped CloudNativePG kind) for the image and upgrade panels. Adds a second, read-only ClusterRole limited to that kind. Without it the UI says "catalog not readable". |
| console.rbac.create | bool | `true` | Render the Roles, ClusterRoles, bindings and the revocation ConfigMap. Turn it off only if you manage them yourself; the authority the console needs is documented in the README. |
| console.rbac.podLogs | bool | `true` | Grant `get pods/log` in the watched namespaces (the bounded log tail and the log-based diagnostics). Withhold it to run without logs. |
| console.rbac.operatorKinds | string | `"auto"` | Grant read on the operator's kinds (PgAdmin, EvidenceAgent, PgAccessRequest) for the console's link-outs. `auto`: when the cluster serves `pgtoolbox.fyannk.dev/v1alpha1` (with `helm template`, pass `--api-versions` or set `true`). The console runs without them. |
| console.logs.streamEnabled | bool | `true` | Follow each member container's log continuously so the diagnostics log matcher sees every line. It keeps only what matched and stores no log text. Needs `rbac.podLogs`. |
| console.logs.matchMaxAge | string | `"6h"` | How long a log observation lasts after its last matching line (10m to 48h). |
| console.service.type | string | `"ClusterIP"` | Service type. |
| console.service.port | int | `80` | Service port. |
| console.port | int | `3000` | Port the console serves its API and UI on. |
| console.probePort | int | `3001` | Port of `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` (plain HTTP unless `tls.secretName` is set). `/metrics` needs a token that may `get` that URL. |
| console.exposure.type | string | `"none"` | How the Service is exposed outside the cluster: `none`, `ingress`, `route` (OpenShift) or `httpRoute` (Gateway API). |
| console.exposure.host | string | `""` | Host name the Ingress, Route or HTTPRoute answers to. Required with any exposure type other than `none`. |
| console.exposure.sse.timeout | string | `"1h"` | Idle timeout the edge is configured with, for the event stream (SSE) the console keeps open. |
| console.exposure.sticky.enabled | bool | `true` | Render cookie affinity for the exposure: ingress-nginx's annotations on the Ingress and Traefik's on the Service (each controller ignores the other's; for another controller, put its own in `ingress.annotations`). An OpenShift Route is sticky by default (`false` disables its cookie). Gateway API session persistence is not in the standard channel: set it on the gateway. |
| console.exposure.sticky.cookieName | string | `"pgtoolbox-console-replica"` | Name of the affinity cookie. It identifies a replica, nothing of the session. |
| console.exposure.ingress.className | string | `""` | `ingressClassName` of the Ingress. Empty uses the cluster's default class. |
| console.exposure.ingress.annotations | object | `{}` | Annotations of the Ingress (controller settings, cert-manager issuer). |
| console.exposure.ingress.tls | object | `{"enabled":false,"secretName":""}` | TLS of the Ingress: `enabled` and the `secretName` of the kubernetes.io/tls Secret that holds the certificate. |
| console.exposure.route.annotations | object | `{}` | Annotations of the OpenShift Route. |
| console.exposure.route.termination | string | `"edge"` | TLS termination of the Route: `edge`, `reencrypt` or `passthrough`. |
| console.exposure.httpRoute.parentRefs | list | `[]` | Gateways the HTTPRoute attaches to, as Gateway API `parentRefs`: `[{name: gw, namespace: infra}]`. |
| console.exposure.routerNamespace | string | `"openshift-ingress"` | Namespace the ingress controller runs in, the one place the NetworkPolicy lets reach the Pod for `ingress` and `httpRoute` exposure: `ingress-nginx` for the community controller. Not used for `route`: the policy then admits the namespaces labelled `policy-group.network.openshift.io/ingress`, which the OpenShift routers, host-network ones included, carry. Used only when the NetworkPolicy is enabled. |
| console.networkPolicy.enabled | bool | `false` | Render a NetworkPolicy for these pods. Off by default: whether the cluster enforces policies, and whether this namespace wants one, is the installing admin's decision. |
| console.networkPolicy.apiServer.mode | string | `"addresses"` | How egress to the API server is allowed. `addresses`: the addresses of the addresses you list in `apiServer.addresses`, or, with `apiServer.lookup`, those of the `kubernetes` EndpointSlice read at install time (deprecated default, see `apiServer.lookup`). `any`: any address on `apiServer.ports`, the fallback for API servers behind a load balancer whose address is not in the EndpointSlice. |
| console.networkPolicy.apiServer.addresses | list | `[]` | API server IP addresses to allow when `apiServer.mode` is `addresses`: the ClusterIP and endpoints of `kubectl get endpointslice kubernetes -n default` (a namespace admin usually cannot read that object: ask the cluster admin). |
| console.networkPolicy.apiServer.lookup | bool | `true` | With `mode: addresses` and no `addresses`, read them from the `kubernetes` EndpointSlice of the `default` namespace at install time. NOTES warns while it is used. The NEXT MINOR DEFAULTS IT TO false: list `addresses`, set `mode: any`, or keep `lookup: true` as a cluster admin. | pgadmin.configDatabase.existingSecret | string | `""` | Secret of the release namespace holding pgAdmin's settings database URI, e.g. `postgresql://pgadmin:<percent-encoded password>@orders-rw:5432/pgadmin?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=system`. The URI must be self-contained: the Pod's libpq defaults (the declared servers' CA bundle, the passfile) are not applied to it by the registration sidecar, so name `sslmode` (and a root certificate the image trusts, or `sslmode=require`) in the URI. Control characters are refused; quote or backslash are escaped for pgAdmin but refused by the registration, so percent-encode them. Read by the kubelet (`secretKeyRef`) into an init container that writes it, owner only, to the Pod's run volume for pgAdmin (`PGADMIN_CONFIG_CONFIG_DATABASE_URI_FILE`), never through the API, so the Pod's Role does not name it and the Deployment never holds it. Changing the Secret needs a Pod restart. Empty: SQLite on a PVC. Set at install: moving an existing SQLite database into PostgreSQL is a manual step with pgAdmin's own tooling. |
| pgadmin.configDatabase.key | string | `"CONFIG_DATABASE_URI"` | Key of the Secret holding the URI. |
| pgadmin.configDatabase.cluster | string | `""` | Name of the CloudNativePG Cluster that holds the settings database. With `networkPolicy.enabled` and `existingSecret`, the policy opens PostgreSQL (5432) to that Cluster's pods, which the declared `servers` may not name. The chart cannot read the URI (the kubelet does), so it cannot find the host itself. Alternative: allow the database in `networkPolicy.extraEgress`. With neither, the chart refuses to render. |
| pgadmin.configDatabase.pooler | string | `""` | Name of the Pooler (cnpg.io/poolerName) in front of the settings database, when the URI goes through one. Same rules as `cluster`. |

| pgadmin.storage.keep | bool | `true` | Keep the volume on `helm uninstall` (`helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`). |
| pgadmin.backups.keep | int | `3` | Copies of the settings database kept next to it on the volume, taken before the first start of a new pgAdmin image. |
